overview: Systematic review of extended community pharmacy opening with a random-effects meta-analysis of net annual budget impact and a narrative summary of views.
population: Populations served by community pharmacies in high-income health systems.
exposure: Extended weekday evening or Sunday opening compared with usual hours.
procedures: Search of four bibliographic sources and grey literature from 2005; screening by one analyst with 20 percent checked by a second reviewer; extraction of budget impact per 100,000 population per year; random-effects pooling.

outcomes.name: Net annual budget impact per 100,000 population
outcomes.measure: Pooled difference between scheme cost and valued offsets for the payer
outcomes.timing: Per year, up to three years

outcomes.name: Reporting completeness
outcomes.measure: Share of studies reporting perspective, price year and offsets
outcomes.why: Determines whether estimates can be compared.

feasibility: One analyst for six months; a second reviewer for 20 percent of screening from the public health team.
biasMitigation: Second reviewer for a sample of screening and all extraction of budget figures
Funding source of each study extracted

biasFlags.label: Sponsorship by pharmacy bodies
biasFlags.note: Many studies are funded by advocates of extended hours.

flags: Pooling depends on comparability not yet assessed
parsimony.simplestPath: One pooled budget figure with a narrative summary of views.

summary: Review with meta-analysis of budget impact as specified in the accepted design.
